draft.briefing: Hey, you're at Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary! These six islets in the Kaveri were formed when a king of Mysore built an embankment across the river between 1645 and 1648, and birds soon moved in.
draft.hungryLine: I don't have food spots for the sanctuary, so plan a meal in nearby Srirangapattana or Mysore.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The Obelisk Monument in Srirangapatna, a memorial to the 1799 siege, is a short drive away.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Settle in by the Kaveri and watch the birds on the islets, this is the largest bird sanctuary in Karnataka.
moodReplies.surprise-me: It was the ornithologist Salim Ali who persuaded the king of Mysore to protect the islets in 1940.

spots.name: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary
spots.detail: Right here · Six islets on the Kaveri full of nesting birds

spots.name: Obelisk Monument
spots.detail: Short drive · Memorial to the 1799 siege of Srirangapatna

legends.title: Pakshi Kashi
legends.body: Locals call this place the Pakshi Kashi of Karnataka. It's the biggest bird sanctuary in the state.

tips.title: Pair it with Srirangapattana.
tips.body: The historic town is only 3 km away.

tips.title: Mysore is close.
tips.body: The sanctuary is 16 km north of Mysore, an easy half-day trip.

story.title: An embankment
story.body: King Kanteerava Narasimharaja Wadiyar built an embankment across the Kaveri between 1645 and 1648. It created 25 islets that soon drew birds.

story.title: The siege nearby
story.body: Close by, the siege of Srirangapatna on 4 May 1799 ended the last Anglo-Mysore war. The Obelisk Monument, built in 1907, remembers those who died.

story.title: Salim Ali steps in
story.body: Salim Ali saw that the islets were a key nesting ground and persuaded the king of Mysore to declare them protected in 1940.

story.title: Ramsar site
story.body: On 15 February 2022 the sanctuary was designated a protected Ramsar site.

story.title: Still growing
story.body: The Karnataka Forest Department looks after it and is buying nearby private land to expand it. About 3 lakh people visited in 2016-17.
